procedure.description: pembrolizumab injection, 200 mg, first-line therapy for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer

denial.carcText: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer.
denial.text: Copperfield Health denied the claim for HCPCS J9271 (pembrolizumab injection, 200 mg, first-line therapy for metastatic non-small cell lung cancer) with date of service 2026-02-26. CARC 56: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer. Payer remark: Use of this agent is considered investigational for the submitted diagnosis.

criteria.text: Histologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer that is metastatic (stage IV) or recurrent and not amenable to curative treatment.
PD-L1 tumor proportion score of 50 percent or greater for single-agent therapy (1 percent or greater when combined with platinum chemotherapy).
No EGFR sensitizing mutation and no ALK rearrangement, since targeted therapy is first-line for those tumors.
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0 to 2.
No prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease.

chart.text: Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.9, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 17 and 13. No ocular pathology noted.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.
Core needle biopsy, right upper lobe mass: adenocarcinoma, TTF-1 positive, napsin A positive, p40 negative. Consistent with primary lung adenocarcinoma.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.

Here with a cough and congestion for 5 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

PET/CT: 4.3 centimeter hypermetabolic right upper lobe mass, hypermetabolic right hilar and subcarinal nodes, two hypermetabolic hepatic lesions in segments 6 and 7, and a lytic hypermetabolic lesion in the left iliac wing. Stage IV disease.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 198, LDL 125, HDL 50, triglycerides 114. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

PD-L1 immunohistochemistry (22C3): tumor proportion score 90 percent. Next-generation sequencing: EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, KRAS G12C, MET exon 14, RET, and NTRK: no actionable alteration detected. Tumor mutational burden 9 per megabase.

59 year old man seen in medical oncology with his daughter. Presented with three months of cough and 12 pounds of weight loss. Long discussion of goals: he wants treatment aimed at living longer and feeling well. Former smoker, 35 pack years, quit 9 years ago. His history otherwise: osteoarthritis of the hands, seasonal allergies. Allergies: codeine makes him sick. Quit smoking 7 years ago, no alcohol, drives for a living. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Stage IV lung adenocarcinoma with liver and bone metastases. Not a surgical or curative radiation candidate. ECOG 1. Still working part time, walks the dog every morning, some fatigue by evening and a cough. No prior systemic therapy. This is first-line treatment for metastatic disease.
A1c came back 6.4. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. He is motivated.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Thoracic tumor board. Case presented. Consensus: single-agent immunotherapy first-line given the biomarker profile and performance status, palliative radiation to the iliac lesion if it becomes painful. Molecular results reviewed by the group.
Vitamin D came back 19. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Back to review the plan. Consented for pembrolizumab 200 milligrams every 3 weeks. Reviewed immune-related side effects, what to call about, and the port placement scheduled for later this week. Vitals today 142 over 87, pulse 68.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 5 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Infusion visit, cycle 1 day 1. Vitals stable, labs acceptable, pembrolizumab 200 milligrams intravenous over 30 minutes, tolerated without reaction. Return in 3 weeks.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 56 denial can be answered from the record.
